concepts.title: Functions and the Elementary Families
concepts.summary: Functions as mappings with a domain and a range, then the families the rest of the discipline uses constantly: affine, quadratic, polynomial, exponential, logarithmic, and trigonometric, with composition and inverses. This lesson absorbs the precalculus the discipline assumes.

concepts.title: Limits: Intuition and the Formal Definition
concepts.summary: What it means for f(x) to approach a value, first through tables and graphs and then through the epsilon-delta definition, with one-sided limits and the cases where a limit does not exist.

concepts.title: Limit Laws and Indeterminate Forms
concepts.summary: The algebraic laws that let limits be computed instead of guessed, the squeeze theorem, and how factoring and rationalizing resolve the indeterminate forms 0/0 and infinity over infinity.

concepts.title: Limits at Infinity and Asymptotic Growth
concepts.summary: Limits as x grows without bound, horizontal and vertical asymptotes, and the dominance hierarchy of logarithms, polynomials, and exponentials, which is the calculus underneath the formal statement of Big-O.

concepts.title: Continuity and the Intermediate Value Theorem
concepts.summary: Continuity at a point and on an interval, the kinds of discontinuity, and the Intermediate Value Theorem, the existence guarantee behind bisection search.

concepts.title: The Derivative as a Rate of Change
concepts.summary: The derivative as the limit of a difference quotient: instantaneous rate of change, slope of the tangent line, best local linear approximation, and the functions where it fails to exist.

concepts.title: Differentiation Rules and the Chain Rule
concepts.summary: The power, product, quotient, and chain rules, derived from the limit definition, with the chain rule read as a composition of local linear approximations.

concepts.title: Derivatives of Exponentials, Logarithms, and Trigonometric Functions
concepts.summary: Why e is the base whose exponential is its own derivative, the derivatives of logarithms and trigonometric functions, and implicit and logarithmic differentiation for expressions the basic rules do not reach.

concepts.title: The Mean Value Theorem and Monotonicity
concepts.summary: Rolle's theorem and the Mean Value Theorem, and what they justify: a positive derivative means increasing, and a zero derivative on an interval means constant.

concepts.title: Extrema, Concavity, and Optimization
concepts.summary: Critical points, the first and second derivative tests, concavity and inflection points, and how to turn a word problem into an optimization on a closed interval.

concepts.title: L'Hôpital's Rule
concepts.summary: L'Hôpital's Rule for 0/0 and infinity over infinity, when its hypotheses fail, and how to rewrite the other indeterminate forms so it applies, including comparing growth rates.

concepts.title: Antiderivatives and Initial-Value Problems
concepts.summary: Reversing differentiation: the family of antiderivatives, the constant of integration, and how an initial condition picks a single solution.

concepts.title: The Definite Integral and Riemann Sums
concepts.summary: Area as the limit of Riemann sums, the left, right, and midpoint rules, the formal definition of the definite integral, and its basic properties.

concepts.title: The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus
concepts.summary: The two parts of the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, which tie accumulation to rates of change and reduce a definite integral to evaluating an antiderivative.

concepts.title: Integration by Substitution and by Parts
concepts.summary: Substitution as the chain rule run backwards and integration by parts as the product rule run backwards, with how to choose the substitution and the parts.

concepts.title: Applications: Area, Volume, and Average Value
concepts.summary: Setting up integrals for the area between curves, volumes by slicing and by revolution, and the average value of a function over an interval.

concepts.title: Improper Integrals
concepts.summary: Integrals over unbounded intervals or of unbounded functions as limits, convergence and divergence, the p-test, and why a probability density has to integrate to 1 over the whole line.

concepts.title: Sequences and Convergence
concepts.summary: Sequences as functions on the natural numbers, the formal definition of convergence, and the monotone convergence theorem for bounded sequences.

concepts.title: Arithmetic and Geometric Progressions
concepts.summary: Arithmetic and geometric progressions, closed forms for their terms and finite sums, and where they appear in computing: loop counts, the amortized cost of a doubling array, and compound growth.

concepts.title: Infinite Series and Partial Sums
concepts.summary: An infinite series as the limit of its partial sums, the geometric series, telescoping sums, the divergence test, and why the harmonic series diverges.

concepts.title: Convergence Tests
concepts.summary: The comparison, integral, ratio, root, and alternating series tests, absolute versus conditional convergence, and how to choose a test for a given series.

concepts.title: Power Series and the Radius of Convergence
concepts.summary: Power series as functions, the radius and interval of convergence, and term-by-term differentiation and integration.

concepts.title: Taylor and Maclaurin Series with Error Bounds
concepts.summary: Taylor and Maclaurin series, the remainder and its error bound, and how many terms a target accuracy requires, which is the base of numerical approximation.

concepts.title: Functions of Several Variables and Level Curves
concepts.summary: Functions of two or more variables, their domains, graphs, and level curves, and limits and continuity when a point can be approached along many paths.

concepts.title: Partial Derivatives and the Multivariable Chain Rule
concepts.summary: Partial derivatives, the tangent plane as the linear approximation, and the multivariable chain rule for compositions through intermediate variables.

concepts.title: Directional Derivatives and the Direction of Steepest Ascent

related.label: Gradients: Extending Derivatives to Several Variables

concepts.summary: Deepens the existing gradients lesson without repeating it: the directional derivative, why the gradient points in the direction of steepest ascent, and why it is perpendicular to level curves.

concepts.title: Critical Points and the Second-Derivative Test
concepts.summary: Critical points of functions of two variables, the second-derivative test through the Hessian, saddle points, and absolute extrema on a closed region.

concepts.title: Polar Coordinates
concepts.summary: Polar coordinates, conversion to and from Cartesian form, curves such as circles, cardioids, and roses, and area in polar form.

concepts.title: Double Integrals, Cartesian and Polar
concepts.summary: Double integrals over rectangles and general regions, iterated integrals and Fubini's theorem, changing the order of integration, and the switch to polar coordinates that evaluates the Gaussian integral.

concepts.title: Triple Integrals
concepts.summary: Triple integrals in Cartesian, cylindrical, and spherical coordinates, with volume and mass as the applications and the Jacobian determinant as the scaling factor of a change of variables.

concepts.title: Differential Equations and Initial-Value Problems
concepts.summary: What a differential equation is, order and solutions, initial-value problems, slope fields, and exponential growth and decay as the first model.

concepts.title: Separable Differential Equations
concepts.summary: Separation of variables, the logistic equation, Newton's law of cooling, and checking a solution by substituting it back.

concepts.title: Choosing a Calculus Tool: A Decision Guide
concepts.summary: A decision guide for the whole discipline: given a problem, choose between limits, derivatives, integrals, series, and multivariable tools, and recognize the trap each one sets.
